name: month-schedule
description: Month grid that shows dated events inside each day, with a type legend and a small-screen agenda — the schedule counterpart to Calendar's date picker.
designIntent: Directories need to show events inside days, not just pick one. MonthSchedule reuses Calendar's date utilities (ISO keys, calendarWeeks, explicit today) so server-rendered pages stay deterministic, and collapses to an agenda list below a breakpoint where day cells get too cramped.

props.name: events
props.description: Events to place inside days; each is dated via getDate.

props.name: getDate
props.description: ISO date key (YYYY-MM-DD) for an event.

props.name: getLabel
props.description: Short label shown on the day chip and in the agenda.

props.name: getType
props.description: Optional type key used for chip color and legend matching.

props.name: month
props.description: Controlled month as YYYY-MM; falls back to defaultMonth, then today.

props.name: onMonthChange
props.description: Called with the new YYYY-MM when paging.

props.name: today
props.description: Override "today" for deterministic server rendering and tests.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP-47 locale for month, weekday and agenda labels.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: 0 starts the week on Sunday, 1 on Monday.

props.name: maxPerDay
props.description: Maximum event chips per day before collapsing into "+N more".

props.name: legend
props.description: Type key → label entries rendered as a legend; also fixes chip tones deterministically.

props.name: agendaBreakpoint
props.description: Below this breakpoint an agenda list replaces the day grid.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description: Custom link element for event hrefs (Next Link, react-router).

props.name: linkHrefProp
props.description: Prop name used to pass the destination to linkComponent.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes merged onto the root container.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name for the month grid; defaults to the month label.

examples.title: Competition calendar
examples.code:
<MonthSchedule
  events={competitions}
  getDate={(c) => c.startDate}
  getLabel={(c) => c.name}
  getType={(c) => c.kind}
  getHref={(c) => '/competitions/' + c.slug}
  legend={[
    { type: 'competition', label: 'Competition' },
    { type: 'workshop', label: 'Workshop' },
  ]}
  today={todayKey}
/>
examples.description: Month grid with typed event chips; tapping an event navigates to its detail page.

examples.title: Controlled month with URL state
examples.description: Keep the visible month in the URL so the schedule is shareable and back-button safe.

antiPatterns.title: Don't use it to pick a date
antiPatterns.explanation: MonthSchedule shows events inside days; it has no selection model. Use Calendar or DatePicker when the user must choose a day.

antiPatterns.title: Don't compute today on the server
antiPatterns.explanation: Without an explicit today prop the component reads the client clock; pass today from a deterministic source for SSR and tests.

accessibility.implementation: Day cells use role=grid/gridcell/row with column headers; today gets aria-current=date
accessibility.userRequirements: The grid conveys month structure to screen readers

accessibility.implementation: Below agendaBreakpoint the grid is replaced by a labelled list of days and events, which is easier to scan than cramped cells
accessibility.userRequirements: Both representations stay in the DOM; CSS picks one per viewport

accessibility.implementation: The month name sits in an aria-live=polite region so paging is announced
accessibility.userRequirements: Keyboard and screen-reader users hear month changes

guidelines: Keep getLabel short — chips truncate; put detail in the destination page
Legend labels describe the type, not the event
badExamples: Fall Classic 2026 — two-day ballroom competition with six heats

compositionRules.relationship: Sibling components sharing the same date utilities; Calendar picks a day, MonthSchedule shows events in days
Day chips and the legend render as sm Badges with deterministic outline tones per type
Pair with ListToolbar and Pagination when the schedule is one view of a filterable directory
